items.title: The Three Little Pigs and the Smart City
items.excerpt: What if the three little pigs lived in a modern smart city? A tale of teamwork, technology, and quick thinking.
items.body:
Once upon a time, in a very modern city, there lived three little pigs. But these pigs weren't building houses of straw, sticks, and bricks — they were building smart homes!

The first pig built a house with automatic lights and voice-controlled doors. The second pig built a house with solar panels and a robot butler. The third pig, being the wisest, built a house with a full security system connected to the city's smart grid.

When a sneaky wolf tried to hack into their homes, the first two pigs' systems failed. But the third pig's house was protected by the city's AI network — and the wolf couldn't get in!

The three pigs learned that being smart isn't about having the fanciest gadgets. It's about thinking ahead and working together.

The End.
items.author: Grade 5 Student

items.title: Little Red Riding Hood in the Desert
items.excerpt: A reimagined classic set in the Arabian desert, where Red Riding Hood meets a wise falcon instead of a wolf.
items.body:
Once, in a small village at the edge of the Arabian desert, there lived a girl everyone called Little Red Riding Hood because of the red shawl her grandmother had made her.

One day, her mother asked her to take a basket of dates and fresh bread to her grandmother, who lived on the other side of the dunes.

As Red walked through the desert, she met a wise old falcon perched on a rock. The falcon warned her that a sly desert fox was planning to trick her. He told her to take the longer path around the oasis.

Red listened. She took the falcon's advice — and when the fox tried to trick her near the oasis, she was already too far away.

She reached her grandmother safely, and they shared dates and stories until the sun set over the sand.

The End.
items.author: Grade 5 Student

items.title: Cinderella's Space Adventure
items.excerpt: Cinderella trades her glass slippers for a spacesuit in this intergalactic twist on a beloved fairytale.
items.body:
Cinderella had always dreamed of seeing the stars — not just from her window, but up close.

When a royal space ball was announced on the Moon Station, she knew she had to go. But her stepmother refused to let her.

With the help of her friendly robot-mouse friends, Cinderella built her own spacesuit out of spare parts. She launched herself into orbit just in time for the ball.

At the ball, she danced with the young space prince — until midnight, when her spacesuit's oxygen alarm beeped and she had to rush back to Earth. She left behind one of her astronaut boots.

The prince searched the entire solar system until he found the girl whose foot fit the boot. And they lived happily — exploring the galaxy together.

The End.
items.author: Grade 5 Student

items.title: The Tortoise and the Hare: Robot Race
items.excerpt: An old rivalry returns — but this time, both the tortoise and the hare have built their own racing robots.
items.body:
The tortoise and the hare had been rivals for years. But this time, they decided to settle the score with robots!

The hare built the fastest racing robot the forest had ever seen — shiny, sleek, and very fast.

The tortoise built a slow but steady robot with an unbeatable battery. It never needed to stop and recharge.

On race day, the hare's robot zoomed ahead — until it overheated and shut down. The tortoise's robot kept going, steady and sure.

The tortoise's robot crossed the finish line first. The hare learned that speed isn't everything — patience and planning matter too.

The End.
items.author: Grade 5 Student

items.title: Aladdin and the Digital Lamp
items.excerpt: Aladdin discovers a laptop instead of a magic lamp — and the genie inside has a few surprises of his own.
items.body:
Aladdin was exploring an old market in the city when he found something unusual — an old laptop in a dusty box.

When he opened it, a puff of blue smoke rose from the screen, and a genie appeared!

"I am the Digital Genie," the genie said. "I grant you three digital wishes — but nothing physical. Only knowledge and skills."

Aladdin thought for a moment. His first wish: to speak every language. His second: to be a master coder. His third: to understand any book ever written.

With these gifts, Aladdin didn't need a palace or gold. He became one of the smartest, kindest people in the city — and he used his gifts to help others.

The End.
items.author: Grade 5 Student

items.title: Snow White and the Seven Robots
items.excerpt: A modern retelling where Snow White befriends seven helper robots instead of seven dwarfs.
items.body:
Snow White lived in a high-tech castle with her jealous stepmother, the Queen.

When the Queen's magic mirror told her that Snow White was the kindest person in the kingdom, the Queen ordered her guards to take Snow White far away.

Lost in the forest, Snow White found a small cottage — but instead of seven dwarfs, she found seven friendly helper robots. Each robot had a special skill: one cooked, one cleaned, one repaired, one gardened, one painted, one sang, and one told the best stories.

Snow White stayed with the robots and taught them about kindness, friendship, and laughter. In return, they protected her and kept her safe.

When the Queen finally found Snow White, the robots banded together to defend her. The Queen's magic was no match for their teamwork.

Snow White lived happily, surrounded by friends — the robots who had become her family.

The End.
items.author: Grade 5 Student

items.title: My First Day at Albayan
items.excerpt: Looking back at the nervous excitement of walking through the school gates for the very first time.
items.body:
I still remember my first day at Albayan like it was yesterday.

I was so nervous. My hands were sweaty, my heart was racing, and I didn't know anyone. I remember standing at the gate, holding my mother's hand, watching all the other students walk in.

But then something wonderful happened. A girl in my class came up to me and said, "Hi! I'm new too. Want to sit together?"

That simple moment changed everything. We sat together at lunch, played at recess, and by the end of the day, I wasn't nervous anymore. I was excited to come back.

Six years later, that girl is still one of my best friends. Albayan has been my second home ever since.
items.author: Grade 6 Student

items.title: The Friend Who Changed Everything
items.excerpt: A story about the power of friendship and how one person can make a difficult year so much brighter.
items.body:
Last year was a hard year for me. I was struggling with my studies, and I felt like I didn't fit in.

Then I met Reem. She sat next to me in class one day and started talking to me like we'd known each other forever. She didn't care that I was quiet or that I wasn't the best at sports. She just liked me for me.

Reem helped me with my homework. She invited me to her birthday party. She stood up for me when other kids teased me. And slowly, things started to get better.

I learned that one true friend can change everything. Friendship isn't about being popular — it's about finding someone who sees the real you.

Thank you, Reem.
items.author: Grade 6 Student

items.title: When I Learned to Never Give Up
items.excerpt: A personal account of failing at something important — and finding the courage to try again.
items.body:
In Grade 4, I failed my first big math test. I had studied so hard, but I still didn't do well. I felt like a failure.

I wanted to give up. I told my mom I wasn't good at math and never would be. But she told me something I'll never forget: "Failing one test doesn't mean you're a failure. It means you have more to learn."

So I tried again. And again. I asked my teacher for help. I practiced every day. Slowly, my grades improved — and by the end of the year, I got the highest mark in the class.

I learned that failing isn't the end of the story. It's just a chapter. The next chapter is up to you.
items.author: Grade 6 Student

items.title: The Teacher I'll Never Forget
items.excerpt: A tribute to a teacher whose kindness and belief changed the way one student saw themselves.
items.body:
Some teachers teach subjects. But Mrs. Almansoori taught me something more important — she taught me to believe in myself.

When I started Grade 5, I was shy and scared to speak up in class. I thought my ideas weren't good enough. But Mrs. Almansoori saw something in me that I didn't see in myself.

She encouraged me to share my thoughts. She praised my writing. She told me, "Your voice matters."

By the end of the year, I was speaking in front of the whole class. I even joined the school newspaper. Mrs. Almansoori's belief in me changed my life.

I'll never forget her. And I hope one day I can be that person for someone else.
items.author: Grade 6 Student

items.title: What I Want to Be When I Grow Up
items.excerpt: A reflection on dreams for the future and the people, places, and moments that inspired them.
items.body:
When I grow up, I want to be a doctor. But not just any doctor — a children's doctor, so I can help kids feel better when they're scared.

I got this idea when I was in the hospital for a week in Grade 3. The nurses and doctors were so kind to me. They made a scary situation feel safe. I want to be that person for someone else one day.

I know it won't be easy. Becoming a doctor takes years of hard work and study. But I'm ready for the challenge. I already read books about the human body, and I love science class.

Whatever I become, I hope I'll always remember what it feels like to be a kid — and to be kind to everyone I meet.
items.author: Grade 6 Student

items.title: Goodbye, Albayan
items.excerpt: A heartfelt farewell letter from a Grade 6 student reflecting on six unforgettable years.
items.body:
Dear Albayan,

I can't believe it's time to say goodbye. Six years ago, I walked through your gates for the very first time — small, scared, and excited.

You taught me so much. Not just math and science and English — but how to be a friend, how to be brave, how to be kind. You gave me teachers who believed in me, friends who laughed with me, and memories I'll carry forever.

I'm ready for the next chapter — for middle school, for new challenges, for the big world out there. But I'll never forget where I came from.

Thank you, Albayan. For everything.

With love,
A Grade 6 Graduate
items.author: Grade 6 Student
